updates.title: LangChain adds browser use and asynchronous subagents to Managed Deep Agents
updates.whatChanged: LangChain released Managed Deep Agents v0.10 on 29 October with managed browser tools and asynchronous subagents. Browsers run in LangSmith sandboxes, use thread- or user-scoped sessions, and support handoff for sign-in. Background subagents run while the agent continues its conversation. Managed Deep Agents remains in public beta.
updates.whyCare: You can support tasks on sites without APIs and long-running parallel work in one managed runtime. Session-scoped login reuse and human handoff add identity and security considerations.
updates.before: Managed Deep Agents subagents waited inline, and agents lacked a managed browser for sites without APIs.
updates.after: Agents can browse with isolated conversation sessions or verified user-scoped logins, request human control for sign-in, and run subagents in the background while continuing the conversation.
updates.learn: Use APIs where they cover the task. Test browser scope, login reuse and handoff before enabling production actions. Check trace visibility and async task completion and cancellation.

sources.name: LangChain - Managed Deep Agents v0.10: Browser use and asynchronous subagents

updates.architectureImplication: Managed browser controls reduce runtime work but widen the action surface. Compare LangChain's sandbox and session controls with options such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser before choosing a managed runtime.
